capabilities: Mark style issues (passive voice, adverbs, hedges, weasel words, clichés, doubled words, long sentences) in the editor
Show a Flesch reading grade in the status bar or panel
Mask code, math, frontmatter, URLs and wikilinks before analysis
Navigate to the next or previous mark via a legend with live counts
Detect repeated words and phrases and compare revision metrics (Pro)
disambiguation: Not a grammar or spell checker; it only highlights patterns that can be tightened and never edits the note.
extras: Freemium: free tier with all seven style marks and reading grade; Pro is a $12 one-time unlock (de-slop marks, echo detector, revision delta, focus mode). English only, works fully offline with no network calls. Listed as Optional payments in the community directory; 14-day refund policy.
problem: Obsidian has no in-editor prose-level style feedback; writing tools either make you leave the editor or lint raw Markdown syntax instead of actual prose.

relations.evidence: For grammar and spelling, LanguageTool and Harper are the right tools, and they sit happily alongside this.
